institution: IIITDM Jabalpur (PDPM Indian Institute of Information Technology, Design and Manufacturing, Jabalpur)
data_source: Careers360 student reviews (aggregated public review data)

key_positive_themes.notes: Modern smart classrooms, advanced laboratories, campus-wide wifi, well-equipped digital and physical library; clean, green, peaceful campus.
Strong, industry-oriented curriculum focused on design, technology, and practical skills; knowledgeable and supportive faculty; regularly updated syllabus.
177+ companies visited in 2020; average salary around 9.9 LPA, median around 8.5 LPA; decent-to-good placement outcomes overall.
Rated 4.0/5 — notably better perceived value compared to some peer IIITs.

key_negative_themes.notes: Hostels described as decent but with room for improvement in maintenance and food quality.
Some reviews note less-experienced faculty in certain departments and inconsistent teaching quality across subjects.
Some older reviews mention placement difficulty during COVID period, with fewer students placed by certain points in the year.

sample_reviews_analyzed.review_snippet: Strong academics with practical and industry focus — modern infra, smart classrooms, good IT facilities
Hostels decent with basic amenities, though maintenance and food quality may need improvement
It is a good college although most faculties are less experienced; placements are decent if not good
177+ companies visited for placements in 2020, average salary 9.9 LPA, median 8.5 LPA
Very few placed till 4th year due to COVID pandemic situation, hoping for the best

conclusion: Sentiment toward IIITDM Jabalpur is strongly positive and the most well-balanced among peer IIITs reviewed, with no single category showing a major weakness. Strengths lie in infrastructure, academics, and value for money, while minor concerns exist around hostel upkeep and variability in faculty experience.
disclaimer: This analysis is based on a sample of publicly available student reviews (Careers360) as of the search date and is illustrative, not a scientifically exhaustive sentiment study.
